user_questions.question: How should 'new merchant' be identified? Options: (A) Opportunity.Type = 'New Business' (only values are New Business / Existing Business) - recommended; (B) the Account has no earlier Onboarding_Application__c; (C) both. Evidence: Opportunity.Type exists with those two values; Onboarding_Application__c.Account__c links applications to accounts; 0 opportunities and 0 applications exist.
user_questions.simulated_answer: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: Access for a new field: design-rules says name exact permission sets/profiles, and org-verification says admins with View All Data still see fields without explicit grants, yet describe run as admin hid every existing custom field on Onboarding_Application__c. The skill does not say whether to add an Admin profile grant; I added an Update Profile Admin row as a judgment call.

Step 5 'predict the answer first': for the 'new merchant' fork I could not predict whether the answer would be 'no preference', and the Type = New Business default is reversible, so the rule arguably said decide rather than ask. The boundary between 'org semantics answer it' (picklist value New Business) and 'evidence points both ways' is unclear.

Testing guidance: a flow whose main outcome is a created related record cannot be asserted by a Flow Test, and 'do not add code only to make something testable' rules out an Apex test; the skill does not state this common case explicitly, so the spec ends up with manual checks only.

Rule 3 two-wrong-claims threshold: AskCoworker's wrong claims (no Account lookup, Automated Process user) were reached after I, but R and T then made a third platform claim (bulk SOQL per interview) that could not be tested with allowed commands; the skill says fall back to documented behavior, which worked, but it is unclear whether R/T should be resent with the correction (skipped because the inventory did not change).
